items.name: AI Canvas
items.description: A launch page for an AI canvas tool: a night-black WebGL infinite canvas that never stops drifting — photos, labelled frames, live pages and an agent at work, with velocity motion blur — washing out to a white page of blur-in scenes, a stepped-word mauve panel, a pinned three-step product walk, gathering multiplayer cursors, an agent wiring a button to its tokens, and one enormous black call to action.
designedFor: AI design, canvas and prototyping tools launching or raising
Products whose pitch is an endless workspace: whiteboards, moodboards, site builders, agent studios
Pages that tell the story one short scene at a time rather than in feature grids
Seeing a WebGL canvas the editor's Motion switch can stop, with every knob as a prop

items.name: Alpine Hotel
items.description: Hotel Arven — a one-page guide to a small, family-run hotel at the top of Zermatt, set like a printed hotel guide on warm paper: a cover with a fill-in availability line, the house's story, a pinned film that splits into the season calendar, a day's timetable with snowboard footage printed inside the type, a rate card, a drawn trail map of nearby spots, arrival routes and what's included, and a registration-card booking form.
designedFor: Small, independent hotels, inns and mountain lodges that take bookings direct
Hospitality brands that want an editorial, printed-matter feel instead of a template
Pages that need real information — seasons, rates, directions, what's included — laid out clearly
Anyone after a paper-textured Lenis + Framer Motion page with pinned video and text-clipped footage

items.name: Arcline — AI CRM
items.description: A minimal, dark five-page site for Arcline, an AI CRM: a hero app window that answers a question live, a sticky five-chapter platform tour with HTML product mockups (table and email composer, workflow builder, pipeline board, analyst, charts), a Deal Memory band with isometric line icons, pricing with a comparison table, customers, an agents page and a changelog.
designedFor: AI and SaaS products that want a calm, precise, hairline-grid landing page
CRM, sales and revenue tools that need to show their product, not describe it
Seeing HTML product mockups, micro-interactions and agent-UI primitives the editor can drive

items.name: Aurel
items.description: A high-end fashion house's site in bone, ink and burnt orange: a film that folds into the header, a garment rising through its headline, sticky split columns, a drifting archive wall and a turning silver seal — across home, collection, product, atelier, journal, house and appointments.
designedFor: Fashion houses, boutiques and ateliers selling a small, considered collection
Editorial landing pages built on sticky, scroll-linked sections
A multi-page shop — collection, product, bag — with every hidden state reachable from the editor
Studying scroll choreography: pinned stages, clip-path reveals, stacking cards and a sideways track

items.name: Castwell — AI Social Media Manager
items.description: A five-page template for a centralized social media manager run by an AI marketing team: floating workflow chips around a serif hero, a product window that unfolds on scroll, a pinned How-it-works tour, an AI Marketing Manager page with a streaming weekly brief, an AI Video Studio with storyboards and templates, a multi-channel scheduler with a best-time heatmap and approvals, and pricing with a comparison table.
designedFor: Social media management, scheduling and creator tools
AI marketing and AI video generation products
SaaS teams that want a calm, editorial, cream-and-ink landing page with night diagram sections
Seeing scroll-pinned tours, pixel wipes and streaming text the editor can drive

items.name: Cirrus — Cloud Dev Environments
items.description: A pixel-matrix site for Cirrus, cloud development environments: white paper under a 9px grid and a palette drawn only as squares — a night server-room hero with CDN packets travelling from origin to edge racks, isometric voxel server cards, a DNA-to-organism-to-tree life cycle for clone/boot/build/ship, a menubar with a pixel-icon product menu, product, network, pricing, changelog and brand-guideline pages, and footers with a different city skyline in line art over a playable Tetris skyline.
designedFor: Developer tools, cloud platforms and infrastructure products
Editorial, argument-led product pages with long reading sections
Pages that want generative pixel art instead of stock illustration
Seeing canvas animations built as editor-controllable components the Motion switch can stop

items.name: Coastal Residence
items.description: Luna Residence — a cinematic one-page site for a small gated development on the coast: an arch that opens onto the hero, a day/night switch, pinned chapters, a sideways coastline story, residence types, amenities and an olive contact footer.
designedFor: Boutique residential developments and off-plan launches selling a handful of homes
Hotels, villas and retreats that want a slow, editorial scroll instead of a booking grid
Studios pitching a premium real-estate concept with pinned, scroll-driven chapters
Anyone after a Lenis + Framer Motion page with a strong condensed-serif voice

items.name: Drape — AI Try-On
items.description: A landing page for an AI fitting room: a three.js hero where every outfit is a pencil sketch drawn by a shader until a selection box opens over it and shows the real garment, a scroll-scrubbed pull-back into a sunlit room, a pinned four-step toolkit that recolours a garment into sixteen colourways in the page, live colour, fit and size controls, stories, parallax features, FAQ and a clay footer.
designedFor: Fashion, retail and AI try-on products that want to show the product working rather than describe it
Seeing a three.js shader carousel, scroll-scrubbed zooms and pinned steps as editor-ready components
Pages that mix a light drafting-paper hero with dark product sections and one warm accent

items.name: Ember Cards
items.description: A dark, metallic landing page for a virtual card company: machined-metal cards (chrome, titanium, champagne, graphite, copper) with brushing, film grain and a pointer-tracked highlight; two live 3D iPhones (React Three Fiber); a manifesto that lights up word by word; a pinned four-step “how it works”; a sideways-scrolling row of use cases; a customer video that zooms to fill the screen; a dotted world map, reviews, an FAQ and a champagne sign-up band.
designedFor: Fintech, card and wallet apps launching with a single clear offer
Mobile-first products that want their app shown on a real 3D phone rather than a flat screenshot
Scroll-told product pages: pinned steps, horizontal rows, a full-bleed video story
Seeing React Three Fiber, Motion and Lenis on one page the canvas editor can pause and edit

items.name: Food Joint
items.description: A loud one-page site for a restaurant: a preloader that flicks through the menu, a hero photo in a morphing SVG cushion under huge type, a scroll-inked statement with food set into the words, a tabbed menu with a pointer-chasing blob preview, a zoom through a word cut out over a wood-fire film, a pinned sideways walk through the kitchen, stickers you can move, and a booking form.
designedFor: Restaurants, burger and fried-chicken joints, bakeries and street-food kitchens with a big personality
Menus that people want to browse, with prices, heat levels and a picture for every dish
Places that sell the kitchen as much as the plate — fire, wood, fryers and films of them
Taking table bookings without a back end on day one

items.name: Glovebox — Car Insurance Manager
items.description: A warm, editorial landing page for Glovebox, an AI that manages car insurance: a pinned hero whose footage a clip-path closes in on while the camera zooms to the centre, three blurred-video feature cards that pin and stack over one another with live task panels, a pinned statistic with work drifting past it, a dot map of members with stories sliding over it, how it works, FAQ and a closing frame that clips open.
designedFor: Insurance, fintech and admin-automation products that want a calm, human, serif-led page
Showing scroll-driven clip-path and video-zoom effects as editor-ready components
Product pages that show an AI working through live task panels rather than describing it

items.name: Halo Support
items.description: A dark, iris-lit landing page for an AI support platform whose agents improve their own metrics — scanline display type, a voice-reactive prompt box that types, thinks and answers, auto-advancing product walkthroughs, a dotted language map and a customer story, authored as named components the editor can read.
designedFor: Launching an AI or agent product that sells on a measurable outcome
A dark, product-led marketing site with live-looking dashboard mockups
Designers who want to restyle atmosphere, type and motion from tokens
Trying the editor's motion and action channels on a motion-heavy page

items.name: Kerfuffle Studio
items.description: A restrained, editorial site for a motion studio: paper and ink with a single accent, one typeface (Instrument Sans) plus a mono for labels, a twelve-column grid with numbered section labels and hairlines. Finished work drops under the cursor in the hero, an ink brush stroke sweeps the screen on every page change, recent projects pile up in a pinned reel, services show a spring-following preview on hover, and the team, a filterable project archive with case studies, a brief form and a full style guide complete it.
designedFor: Animation, film and social-content studios that want the work to do the talking
Editorial portfolio sites built on a strict grid, with motion used sparingly
Multi-page studio sites: home, about, work with case studies, services and contact
Seeing Motion, Lenis and CSS animation on one page the canvas editor can pause, reduce and edit

items.name: Overtime
items.description: A long-read sports magazine on an infinite WebGL canvas: eighty-four athletes on an endless, draggable sheet that clips and motion-blurs as it moves, with a list view, a full-screen gallery, a profile per athlete and an about page with the issue’s writers.
designedFor: Sports magazines, clubs and federations with a face and a profile per athlete
Portfolios and collections that want to be explored by dragging rather than scrolling
Photography or editorial series with dozens to hundreds of square pieces
Seeing a WebGL canvas, a text-first profile page and a dark editorial palette in one project the editor can read

items.name: Photographer Portfolio
items.description: An editorial portfolio for a working photographer: home, portfolio with category filter, a page per gallery, about, services with FAQ, and an enquiry form.
designedFor: Wedding, portrait and editorial photographers showing whole stories rather than single frames
Studios that sell packages and want pricing and FAQs on one page
Anyone who needs an enquiry form without a back end on day one
Starting a multi-page site the editor can read component by component

items.name: Pixelkeep
items.description: A pixel-art secure web gateway site on a golden-ratio type and spacing system: a dusk-sky hero, value proposition, decrypting feature board, a sticky 3D dashboard riding three sections, how it works with a request simulator, case studies, pricing with a seat calculator, a get-started wizard and a random landing-page generator.
designedFor: A pixel-art / 8-bit product or game-adjacent landing page with real depth
Seeing a sticky, scroll-linked dashboard header driving three sections
Pointer-tilt 3D cards, CSS 3D cubes and a radar built from plain transforms
Rolling a random, shareable template from a seed and painting the whole site with it

items.name: Postwise — AI Email
items.description: A sea-glass landing page for Postwise, an AI email assistant: a hero lit by a drifting teal, mint and apricot glow, a hairline numbers band, a deep-lagoon copilot section with floating notes and drifting signals, three how-it-works cards, a clickable feature deck, persona tabs, a team dashboard over a sunlit desk, a results bento, a duotone customer-story carousel, monthly/yearly pricing with a border-beam plan, an FAQ, a wall of love and poster-type calls to action.
designedFor: AI email, inbox and productivity tools
SaaS products that need the full set: numbers, how it works, stories, pricing and FAQ
Sales, support and communication platforms with several audiences to speak to
Seeing a stacked card deck, an Embla carousel, parallax and a border beam built as editor-controllable components

items.name: Riot Folio
items.description: A loud portfolio for an independent builder — electric ultramarine, six saturated project tones, duotone photography, hero cards that fly into the work grid on scroll, odometer stats and a filterable project archive.
designedFor: Designers, engineers and consultants who want a portfolio people remember
Showing a handful of case studies properly and the rest as a searchable archive
A bold, colourful starting point that is still quiet enough to read
Trying scroll-linked motion that the editor can name, tune and pause

items.name: SDK Scaffold
items.description: Quartz, the canvas scaffolding page authored as named React components and opted into @canvas/react — the starting point for a project the editor can read by component.
designedFor: Starting a SaaS or product landing page from a real, responsive layout
Seeing what @canvas/react gives the editor: layers named after components, editable props
Teams who want a Radix + Tailwind v4 baseline to restyle from a DESIGN.md
Trying the editor's motion and action channels on a page that uses them

items.name: Vantage — AI Models
items.description: A sky-blue and white landing page for a frontier AI lab: a serif headline that types its own verb, a live product bento, pixel-mosaic edges that fade into sky washes, one API in three languages, and the sections a launch page needs: steps, reasons to switch, a platform split, testimonials, FAQ and a closing call.
designedFor: AI model, API or developer-platform launch pages
Products with several modalities (chat, code, voice, image, agents) to show at once
Teams who want a calm, white, editorial look instead of a dark gradient hero
Studying editor-ready motion: typed headline, looping previews, count-ups

items.name: Tidemark — Fintech
items.description: A poster-loud fintech landing page for Tidemark, business banking for startups: oxblood, cream, pink and coral, heavy extended caps, square edges and warm moody photography — a photo hero with the account form, a metal card and a live balance strip over the name set edge to edge, a colour-block product grid with working mini-UIs, a treasury yield calculator and chart, security, customer stories, monthly/yearly pricing, an FAQ and a disclosures footer.
designedFor: Fintech, banking, payments and treasury products
B2B SaaS that sells to finance teams and founders
Pages that need a calculator, a chart and honest disclosures beside the marketing
Seeing a count-up, a pointer-driven card and an interactive chart built as editor-controllable components
